propositions: The DC backend needs a TicketTransport built on pycontribs/jira, confined to an opt-in [jira-datacenter] extra and imported lazily so import rebar stays dependency-free and a missing extra raises a clear install-naming error.

Auth uses a Personal Access Token read env-only from JIRA_PAT and passed as token_auth, while url and project come from typed config, and a malformed [tool.rebar.jira] config fails loudly with ConfigError rather than degrading to env-only.
Each transport method returns rebar's raw payload shapes (not jira.Issue), validated against the shared verified-fake shape contract so the DC implementation cannot drift from the Cloud one.

Retry, timeout, and error typing mirror acli_rest exactly: transient faults (including builtin TimeoutError from ssl/socket read-timeouts) retried with 2s/5s backoff, HTTP errors never retried, and unknown assignees raise BackendAssigneeNotFoundError.
The DC backend module must self-register via an import in adapters/__init__.py so select_backend("jira-datacenter") resolves, otherwise it raises BackendRegistryError at runtime.

TLS certificate verification is never disabled: the transport passes options["verify"] as True or a ca_bundle path, allow_insecure affects only the non-https URL scheme check, and resolved_statuses configures the DC absence probe defaulting to {Resolved, Done, Cancelled}.
